1	# Trajectory router — surface-gated, evidence-escalated scored ladder
2	
3	A rule-based model router for agent trajectory logs, plus the analysis that justifies
4	each rule. Built for the Viktor / TUM.ai challenge (22–23 Aug 2026) against a redacted
5	export of real agent trajectories.
6	
7	Stdlib-only at the core. `matplotlib` and `scipy` are needed for the chart and the
8	significance tests, nothing else. No GPU, no API key, no network.
9	
10	---
11	
12	## The finding the router is built on
13	
14	Two questions decided the whole design:
15	
16	**1. Does the harness surface pick the model?** Yes, and near-deterministically.
17	
18	| tools offered | requests | family served |
19	|---|---|---|
20	| `bash` + `file_edit` + slack (12) | 692 | **100% claude** |
21	| `apply_patch` + slack (10) | 224 | **100% gpt** |
22	| `file_read` + `run_shell` (2) | 153 | **mixed** — the only cross-family surface |
23	| msteams + `bash` (17) | 53 | **100% claude** |
24	| msteams + `apply_patch` (15) | 18 | **100% gpt** |
25	
26	**1000 / 1153 requests (87%) sit on a family-locked surface.** All 162 rows containing
27	a `custom_tool_call` and all 318 containing `reasoning` items are gpt. `apply_patch` is
28	a custom tool and `file_edit` is a function tool — *different tool schemas*. Moving a
29	call across families on a locked surface is a harness change, not a routing decision.
30	A router that books those savings is booking something it cannot deliver.
31	
32	**2. Within a surface, does the tier track difficulty?** No.
33	
34	On the 692-request claude surface, the logged model is statistically independent of
35	every difficulty signal measured:
36	
37	| H₀: model ⟂ … | χ² | df | p |
38	|---|---|---|---|
39	| depth (tool calls so far) | 10.75 | 15 | 0.77 |
40	| strict error outputs | 13.43 | 10 | 0.20 |
41	| est. input tokens | 16.32 | 15 | 0.36 |
42	
43	Spearman ρ between difficulty and logged price is +0.014 (p = 0.72). The 224-request
44	gpt surface *does* fail the χ² independence test (p = 0.008 on depth, 0.004 on errors)
45	but its Spearman is −0.050 (p = 0.46) — the dependence is **non-monotone in price**,
46	not a cost/quality ladder. The deepest and most error-prone gpt calls are *more* likely
47	to land on `luna`, the cheapest arm.
48	
49	So: **the platform picks the model from the tool schema, not the task.** Every
50	difficulty-based routing gain is unclaimed. And because assignment is
51	difficulty-independent within a surface, propensities are per-surface constants, there
52	is no confounding to adjust away, and off-policy evaluation is genuinely identified —
53	a rare luxury.
54	
55	Full generated report: `results/policy_report.md`.
56	
57	---
58	
59	## The router
60	
61	```
62	Layer 0   feasibility gates      what this call MAY be routed to   router/surfaces.py
63	Layer 1   scalar difficulty      one knob → a whole frontier       router/features.py
64	Layer 2   one-way escalation     failing loop pins the strong tier router/policy.py
65	```
66	
67	**Layer 0 — gates, learned not assumed.** `SurfaceMap` fits the surface → family map
68	from the log itself: a surface whose logged calls are ≥95% one family is locked to it.
69	Plus the capability gates visible in the export (images, context size). Unseen surfaces
70	fall back to the logged model's family — the conservative choice.
71	
72	**Layer 1 — an additive difficulty score, not a decision tree.** A tree gives one
73	operating point; the deliverable is a frontier. The rules become weights:
74	
75	| term | weight | why |
76	|---|---|---|
77	| `depth / 15` | 0.30 | tool calls already in the loop (p50 = 5, p90 = 22, max = 136) |
78	| `err_recent / 3` | 0.25 | strict errors in the **last 3** outputs — recency beats total |
79	| `thrash / 3` | 0.20 | same tool, same args, again: the model is stuck |
80	| `log10(tokens)` | 0.15 | prefix size |
81	| `n_user_turns > 1` | 0.10 | a second user turn is usually a correction |
82	
83	Every feature is computed from `input` only — state the harness already holds *before*
84	the call — so a router built on them is deployable, not just retrospectively fitted.
85	
86	**Layer 2 — a one-way door.** ≥2 strict errors in the last 3 outputs, or a tool+args
87	repeat, pins the strong tier for the rest of the trajectory. This is the only rule with
88	a causal story rather than a correlational one, and staying pinned also protects the
89	prefix cache on the tail.
90	
91	**What "don't downgrade" means.** By default (`--escalate-to logged`) a call that isn't
92	cheap enough is simply left where production put it, so the router only ever claims
93	*safe downgrades*. `--escalate-to top` raises it to the most capable common arm on that
94	surface instead — defensible only if you accept capability == price, which on this
95	export sends every escalated claude call to the $10 arm and costs **+111%**.
96	
97	---
98	
99	## Results
100	
101	Logged policy: **$87.68** (estimated tokens, assumed price sheet, input only, cache-aware).
102	
103	| q sent cheap | cost | vs logged | downgraded | mean difficulty of downgraded | hard-quartile downgraded |
104	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
105	| 0.00 | $91.93 | +4.9% | 0% | — | 0.00 |
106	| 0.50 | $78.24 | −10.8% | 36% | 0.120 | 0.00 |
107	| **0.75** | **$64.39** | **−26.6%** | 54% | 0.170 | **0.00** |
108	| 0.90 | $52.17 | −40.5% | 64% | 0.214 | 0.41 |
109	| 1.00 | $37.37 | −57.4% | 71% | 0.245 | 0.68 |
110	
111	At q = 0, nothing is downgraded and cost still rises 4.9% — that is Layer 2 alone,
112	upgrading the visibly failing loops. The headline operating point is **q = 0.75:
113	−26.6% cost with the hard quartile untouched.**
114	
115	**Ablations** (at q = 0.70, −22.8% baseline):
116	
117	| variant | cost vs logged | reading |
118	|---|---|---|
119	| full router | −22.8% | — |
120	| `--no-gates` | −37.6% | the gates cost **15 pp of illusory savings** that would need a harness rewrite |
121	| `--no-escalation` | −27.6% | Layer 2 costs **~5 pp** — the price of upgrading failing loops |
122	
123	![frontier](results/frontier.png)
124	
125	---
126	
127	## Honest limits
128	
129	- **There is no quality axis in this data.** No outputs, no `usage`, no labels — and
130	  since assignment is difficulty-independent, there is no quality signal to recover
131	  from the log either. `retention` is a **proxy** (tier conservativeness), not measured
132	  quality, and is labelled as such everywhere it appears.
133	- **`hard_downgrade_exposure` is 0 by construction for q ≤ 0.75** — the metric and the
134	  sweep knob are the same quantile. Read `downgraded_share` and
135	  `mean_difficulty_downgraded` at low q; they stay informative everywhere.
136	- **All token counts are estimates** (chars / 4). The export has no `usage` field.
137	- **Pricing is an assumption.** Model ids are anonymized, so no public price sheet
138	  applies. `pricing.json` holds the assumed rates; swap it and every number re-derives.
139	- **Capability is ranked by price.** No tier order is published. Pass `capability_rank`
140	  to `ScoredLadderRouter` if the organizers publish one.
141	- **The error detector is approximate.** The loose regex fires on 1563/10907 tool
142	  outputs; strict exit-code/traceback markers fire on 459. That gap of 1104 outputs is
143	  the error bar on every error-driven rule. The router uses the strict count.
144	- **Trajectories are barely reconstructable.** Only 153/1153 requests are a strict
145	  item-prefix of another; 929 of 978 groups are singletons. The export samples calls,
146	  it does not contain whole loops — so the cache-reset penalty is *modelled*, not

148	- **3 surface × arm cells have propensity < 2%** (`claude-sonnet-4-6` and
149	  `claude-opus-4-6`) and are unestimable. They are named in the report rather than
150	  silently averaged over.

Built and committed at `D:\Github-Projects\viktor-trajectory-router` (2 commits, pipeline verified end to end against your export).

## What changed from the plan

Two things the data corrected once I ran the analysis properly:

**The gpt surface isn't difficulty-blind — it's difficulty-*dependent in a non-monotone way*.** χ² rejects independence on the 224-request gpt surface (p=0.008 depth, 0.004 errors), but Spearman ρ = −0.05 (p=0.46). The deepest and most error-prone gpt calls are *more* likely to land on `luna`, the cheapest arm. So it's not a cost-quality ladder pointing the right way; it's something else. My earlier "no structure anywhere" claim only held for the claude surface — the report now states both tests, because either alone misleads.

**The escalation target had to change.** Ranking capability by price sends every escalated claude call to `claude-fable-5` at $10/1M, which made the cheap end of the curve cost **+111%** vs logged. Default is now `--escalate-to logged`: absent evidence of trouble, leave the call where production put it, so the router only ever claims *safe downgrades*. Layer 2 still upgrades on evidence, because there the upgrade is earned.

## Results

Logged policy: **$87.68** (estimated tokens, assumed prices, input only, cache-aware).

| q sent cheap | cost | vs logged | downgraded | mean difficulty of downgraded |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.00 | $91.93 | +4.9% | 0% | — |
| **0.75** | **$64.39** | **−26.6%** | 54% | 0.170 |
| 1.00 | $37.37 | −57.4% | 71% | 0.245 |

q=0 costs 4.9% *more* while downgrading nothing — that's Layer 2 alone, upgrading visibly failing loops. Headline: **−26.6% with the hard difficulty quartile untouched**.

Ablations at q=0.70 (−22.8% baseline): `--no-gates` → −37.6%, so **the gates cost 15pp of illusory savings** that would require rewriting the tool schema. `--no-escalation` → −27.6%, so Layer 2 costs ~5pp.

## Two caveats I built into the output rather than hid

- `hard_downgrade_exposure` is **0 by construction** for q ≤ 0.75 — the metric and the sweep knob are the same quantile. I added `downgraded_share` and `mean_difficulty_downgraded`, which stay informative everywhere, and the script prints the warning.
- Tightening the error detector moved the claude-surface error p-value from 0.73 → 0.20 (still independent). Loose regex fires on 1563/10907 outputs, strict on 459; that 1104-output gap is printed as the error bar on every error-driven rule.

## Layout

`router/` — [loader.py](../viktor-trajectory-router/router/loader.py), [features.py](../viktor-trajectory-router/router/features.py), [surfaces.py](../viktor-trajectory-router/router/surfaces.py), [cost.py](../viktor-trajectory-router/router/cost.py), [policy.py](../viktor-trajectory-router/router/policy.py), [quality.py](../viktor-trajectory-router/router/quality.py), [ope.py](../viktor-trajectory-router/router/ope.py)
`scripts/` — extract_features → analyze_policy → route_sweep → plot_frontier, plus [selftest.py](../viktor-trajectory-router/scripts/selftest.py) (10 checks, all passing — the multi-call paths are barely exercised by real data since 929/978 groups are singletons).

Only step 1 touches the export; `.gitignore` excludes `export/`, all `*.jsonl`, and the derived per-request caches. Nothing but aggregates is tracked — I verified with `git ls-files`.

```bash
cd D:/Github-Projects/viktor-trajectory-router && python scripts/route_sweep.py --emit-theta 0.75
```

The quality axis is still a labelled proxy. `router/ope.py` computes SNIPS with ESS and positivity diagnostics the moment you drop in `judged_scores.json` — and it returns `None` rather than a number when you haven't.
